extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, their attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners and staff involved in ex parte reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing and prosecuting appeals, examiner answers, hearings, and disclosure duties in USPTO ex parte reexamination proceedings. Covers timing, brief content requirements, responses to new grounds, duty to disclose, interviews, and judicial review avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination filed on or after November 29, 1999, the patent owner may appeal to the Board only after the final rejection of the claims. A third party requester may not appeal or otherwise participate in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is based on the current version of 35 U.S.C. 134 as amended by Public Law 106-113. For reexaminations filed before November 29, 1999, different appeal options may apply (see MPEP § 2279).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal need not be signed, but the fee required by 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) must accompany the notice of appeal. The period for filing the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally 2 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of a first response to a final rejection having a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the period an additional month (so long as total does not exceed 6 months). Where a notice of appeal is defective the patent owner will be notified (Form PTOL-475) and given a 1-month (or 30 days, whichever is longer) period to cure defects; failure to timely file notice and/or fee results in dismissal (Form PTOL-468) and termination of reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during the appeal period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal brief is not filed, but within the period allowed for filing the brief an amendment is presented which places the claims of the patent in a patentable condition, the amendment may be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments should not be included in the appeal brief. Separate amendments (filed with or after the appeal) are addressed in MPEP § 1207. If an amendment is filed with or after the appeal it is treated as a separate submission under the applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing the appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the appeal brief is 2 months from the date of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to file within that time, the patent owner may file a petition with the appropriate extension of time fee to the CRU or Technology Center requesting additional time (usually 1 month). If sufficient cause is shown and petition filed prior to expiration, the Director may grant up to 1 month; requests for more than 1 month require extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely file appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the brief and/or the appeal brief fee within the permissible time will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-468 is used to notify the patent owner that the appeal is dismissed. Reexamination prosecution is terminated and a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) will be issued indicating status of claims at time of final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief content requirements (37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant shall file a brief of the authorities and arguments on which he or she will rely to maintain the appeal, including a summary of claimed subject matter which must refer to the specification by page and line number, and to the drawing by reference characters, and a copy of the claims involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required; where a third-party requester exists, a copy must be served on that requester. For reexamination, the copy of claims should be double-spaced, start on a new page, and include all underlining and bracketing per 37 CFR 1.530(f); new claims added in reexamination should be completely underlined (departure from MPEP § 1205.02 for applications). The brief and every paper relating to an appeal should indicate the art unit number and reexamination control number. Briefs must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner; a reply brief, if filed, shall be entered, but amendments/affidavits/evidence are subject to 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and completeness of appellant's positions in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board should be provided with a brief fully stating the position of the appellant with respect to each issue involved in the appeal so that no search of the record is required in order to determine that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that appellant considers a ground 'clearly improper' does not justify failing to state the reasons in the brief. If the brief fails to set forth authorities and arguments for any ground, that ground may be summarily sustained. Distinguish between no argument (summary sustainment appropriate) and argument that carries no conviction (decision on merits may still be made, often an affirmance). Appellant must traverse every ground presented for review; oral argument will not remedy failure to traverse in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking Board review of a Substantial New Question (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain Board review of the examiner's SNQ determination, the patent owner must include the SNQ issue and appropriate arguments in its appeal brief to the Board and must have first requested reconsideration of the SNQ issue by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ex parte reexamination proceedings ordered on or after June 25, 2010, the patent owner may seek a final agency decision from the Board on the SNQ only if the patent owner first requested reconsideration before the examiner (e.g., in a patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or response under 37 CFR 1.111) and then seeks review in the appeal. In the brief the SNQ issue and arguments should be presented under a separate heading and identify the communication in which the patent owner first requested reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for determining compliance with 37 CFR 41.37
rubrics_metrics.description: Since May 25, 2010, the Board has sole responsibility for determining whether appeal briefs filed in ex parte reexamination proceedings comply with 37 CFR 41.37 and will complete the determination before forwarding the brief to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination should be completed within approximately one month. If the brief is compliant or contains only minor informalities that do not affect the panel's ability to render a decision, the Board accepts it and forwards it to the examiner. If non-compliant, the Board sends notice requiring a corrected brief to be filed within the time set in the notice to avoid dismissal. The Board also reviews corrected briefs and addresses inquiries/petitions regarding non-compliant notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Board acceptance of appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appeal brief is accepted by the Board as in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal brief will not later be held defective by the CRU or the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will not return or remand the proceeding to the examiner for issues related to a non-compliant appeal brief. Examiners are not required to review briefs for compliance with 37 CFR 41.37; Notification of Non-Compliant Appeal Brief form PTOL-462R and related form paragraphs are not available in OACS for CRU use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of seriously defective briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal brief contains serious defects that will prevent the examiner from drafting an examiner’s answer, the examiner should report the issue to the Director of CRU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of CRU will communicate with the Board regarding the issue if appropriate. Examiners should not hold briefs defective; the Board corresponds directly with appellants on non-compliant brief issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims when appellant identifies fewer than all rejected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the notice of appeal or appeal brief identifies fewer than all of the rejected claims as being appealed, the examiner will treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must maintain all of the rejections set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken unless appellant has overcome the rejection (e.g., by persuasive arguments, acceptable terminal disclaimer, or evidence). In situations where appellant requests holding a rejection in abeyance or presents no argument on a rejection, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and authority for examiner's answer (37 CFR 41.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief. An examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified), unless the examiner's answer expressly indicates a ground has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection; any rejection that relies upon evidence not relied upon in the Office action must be designated as a new ground. The examiner must obtain Director approval to furnish an answer that includes a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant options in response to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer contains a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either (1) request that prosecution be reopened before the primary examiner by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits or other evidence (relevant to the new ground), or (2) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief as set forth in § 41.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to reopen prosecution will be entered and is treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. A reply brief to maintain the appeal must address each new ground (per § 41.37(c)(1)(iv)) and follow other requirements of § 41.37(c); a reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence (if so, treated as reopening prosecution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on extensions of time for reply to examiner's answer/new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the two-month period for responding to an examiner's answer containing a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.136(b) for extensions of time to reply for patent applications and § 1.550(c) for extensions of time to reply for ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner's answers and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appellant files a timely reply brief to an examiner’s answer or a supplemental examiner’s answer, the examiner may (A) acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief, (B) reopen prosecution to respond, or (C) furnish a supplemental examiner’s answer responding to any new issue raised in the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection. A supplemental examiner’s answer (other than to respond to new issues raised in the reply brief) is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board for such purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file a written request accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3) within 2 months after the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant may participate in an oral hearing unless the request and fee have been timely filed. In ex parte reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless appellant petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 (with fee) to have the hearing closed and the petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to courts and third-party limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner dissatisfied with the Board decision may seek judicial review. For reexaminations filed before November 29, 1999 there were options to appeal to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141) or D.C. District Court (35 U.S.C. 145); for reexaminations filed on or after November 29, 1999, appeal is only to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141). A third party requester may not seek judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have permitted intervention by a third party requester in appropriate circumstances, but an intervenor has no standing to appeal the court’s decision. See cited case law in MPEP for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and disclosure in reexamination (37 CFR 1.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding (the patent owner, each attorney or agent who represents the patent owner, and every other individual substantively involved on behalf of the patent owner) has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose all information known to be material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding for each claim pending until that claim is cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty continues throughout the proceeding. Information material to a cancelled claim need not be submitted if not material to any remaining claim. The duty is deemed satisfied if all information known to be material was cited by the Office or submitted in an information disclosure statement. Fraud or bad faith violates this duty. IDS should be filed within two months of the order to reexamine or as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of information 'material to patentability' (37 CFR 1.555(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material when it is not cumulative to information of record and (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination with other patents/printed publications, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance-of-evidence standard, giving each claim term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, before considering any contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) content, timing, and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals are strongly encouraged to file IDSs in accordance with 37 CFR 1.98 within two months of the order to reexamine, or as soon thereafter as possible. An IDS filed under 37 CFR 1.555 by the patent owner after the order and before the first action on the merits may be submitted as part of a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or as a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed as part of a 1.530 statement the submission may include discussion of patentability issues; if filed separately it must be limited to a listing of the information and an explanation of its relevance (discussion of patentability issues in a separate IDS paper is improper). Copies of cited documents must be supplied per 37 CFR 1.98(a): legible copy of each foreign patent; each publication or the relevant portion (other than U.S. patents and published U.S. patent applications unless required); for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the specification including claims and any drawings or the portion which caused it to be listed; and all other information or portions causing it to be listed. The exception in 1.98(d) does not apply to reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for compliance and consequences of noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for compliance with 37 CFR 1.555 rests on the individuals designated (patent owner, attorneys/agents, others substantively involved). The Office will not evaluate compliance during the reexamination proceeding; questions of compliance raised will be noted as unresolved under § 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any fraud or violation of the duty of disclosure through bad faith or intentional misconduct results in noncompliance. Individuals who fail to comply do so at the risk of diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate issuing from the proceeding. See MPEP §§ 2282 and 2686 regarding duty to disclose prior or concurrent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in ex parte reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.560)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and patent owners (or their attorneys/agents) must be conducted in the Office during Office hours at times designated by the examiner; interviews will not be permitted at other times or places without Director authority. Interviews for discussion of patentability of claims will not be conducted prior to the first official action (except limited passive-role amendment situations initiated by the examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. Requests by third-party requesters to participate or attend interviews will not be granted. In every interview, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview must be filed by the patent owner as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action or as a separate paper within one month from the interview date (whichever is later). Telephone interviews by support staff to discuss filing defects may be permitted. Where a panel review was conducted, panel members will be included in interviews where possible. The patent owner's role should be passive if the examiner initiates an interview solely to provide an amendment which will make the claims patentable.
